Rebumped 2026-09-01 for the #802/#807 exact-coordinate fix. The fixture is fully node-aligned (dx=1mm, every dimension an integer mm), so it sat squarely on the defect: under f32 coordinates the patch realized 1008 cells (28x36 - hi-face node planes included against the documented [lo,hi) convention); the exact-f64 builder realizes 945 cells (27x35, convention-exact). f_res 1940.695660 -> 1994.994938 MHz (+54.299 MHz, +2.80%), matching the patch losing one cell plane on its 36mm resonant side (dL/L = 1/36 = +2.78%) - sign and size are the mechanism witness. s11 dip -69.9163 -> -68.3214 dB; dip frequency 3496.672 -> 3321.838 MHz (informational only - the dip is a probe-feed match artifact, not a gated mode; dips measure match, not existence). The previous baseline pinned the f32-accident realization; per #802 the convention realization is authoritative. Prior note (2026-08-23, #638 CPML-pad attribution) retained below.

_correction_717_lane_signal: Correction 2026-09-13 (#717 item 1). One sentence in _note is false: "Drift went unnoticed because slow_physics runs at release tags only and none was cut between 2026-07-28 (v1.6.7) and 2026-08-23." The weekly scheduled workflow selected slow_physics throughout that window. Its slow lane passes -m on the pytest command line, and a command-line -m REPLACES pyproject's addopts marker expression ('not gpu and not slow and not slow_physics') rather than intersecting with it, so slow and slow_physics are selected there and nowhere else on a schedule; at v1.6.7 the lane read -m "not gpu" (validation.yml:41 at that tag) against that same addopts line (pyproject.toml:73 at that tag). Checked directly on 2026-09-13: python -m pytest --collect-only tests/locks/test_sheet_resonance_position_ab.py collects nothing under the default addopts (1 deselected) and collects its one slow_physics test under -m "not gpu and not highmem". What was missing was the signal, not the run: gh run list --workflow=validation.yml shows the last green scheduled run was 2026-06-29, and every scheduled run after it (2026-07-06 through 2026-09-07, nine failures plus the 2026-08-24 cancellation) filed no issue, no comment and no notification -- the three scheduled runs inside this fixture's drift window (08-03, 08-10, 08-17) all ended in failure. That is the hole #717 is about, and the notify job added to .github/workflows/validation.yml is the fix. Only that one causal sentence is corrected here; the measured numbers, the bisect and the #638 attribution in _note are untouched, and _retired_by_931_fixture_repair still owns the separate geometry claims it retires.
